````text
# #2688: Patch: the AI prices a Unit's “when this attacks” and “after this attacks” effects while it stands on the board
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Some Units do something every time they attack: The Propagation's Wasp makes a copy of itself, Badger and Honey Badger grow, Boots on the Ground and Nature Titan have their own payoffs. The practice AI does see the effect when it plans its own attack this turn, but when it weighs a Unit sitting on the board, its own or the opponent's, it values it as a plain body. So it kills a vanilla 4/4 and leaves the Wasp that doubles next turn, and it trades its own Badger away like a plain body. Once built, the AI counts what a Unit's next attack would give its controller, as it already counts what its start-of-turn or end-of-turn text would give.

## Why
- The hooks are `when_attacks` and `after_attack` (`crates/engine/src/script.rs:1190-1205`). Ten non-token Units carry one (grep `when_attacks: Some|after_attack: Some` under `crates/cards/src/scripts`), among them Boots on the Ground `classic-013`, Nature Titan `classic-045`, Badger `stinkyscape-075`, Honey Badger `stinkyscape-076`, Wasp and Hornet `stinkyscape-091`/`092` and Shield Amplifier `stinkyscape-038`.
- Nothing in `crates/ai/src` reads either hook. `unit_worth` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:333-390`) adds the Activate price (R2564000), Plague Counters, Death (R2424000) and turn hooks (R2477000, R2565000), all probed once at the decision's root and stored in `Prices`.
- The reply's trader picks the opponent's attacks by `kill_worth`, which is `unit_worth` less Death and Reborn (`evaluate.rs:1092-1099`, `crates/ai/src/reply.rs:146-156`, `:209-245`), so an attack hook never changes which body it removes first.
- Honey Badger is on the sweep's at-risk list (`crates/ai/src/shadow_ban.rs:855`).

## Proposal
- A root probe in the shape of the Activate probe (`probe_turns`, `evaluate.rs:1603-1622`): for each readable Unit on either field with an attack hook, at its controller's next turn on a sandbox copy, declare its attack on the enemy hero where legal (else the first legal target), and the same attack by a twin with the hooks stripped (its printed keywords kept); the controller's evaluation difference is the price, stored in `Prices.attack_hooks`.
- `unit_worth` adds `w.attack_hook * price` inside the Brittle share; a new `AI_EVAL.attack_hook` weight in `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (CLAUDE.md rule 9). The trader and `even_trade` then read it through `kill_worth`.
- Draw probe nodes from the existing death/turn-hook budget or a new named one; nothing hidden is probed (R185).
- A ruling in this issue's block, with `spec/pending/<issue>.md`; re-run `cargo jackioh gate`.

## Where it lands
- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, `crates/ai/src/decide.rs` (where the root probes are gathered)
- Tests: a new `crates/ai/tests/ai/attack_hooks.rs` beside `turn_hooks.rs`
- `spec/rulings/R<n>.md`, `spec/pending/<issue>.md`; SPEC §6.2, §9.9

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Facing an enemy Wasp and a vanilla Unit of equal stats with one removal, the AI removes the Wasp.
- [ ] The AI's own Badger is worth more on its board than a vanilla body of the same stats.
- [ ] With a zero `attack_hook` weight the evaluation is what it is today (a test pins it).
- [ ] Tests named after the new ruling, listed in its `proven_in`; `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, clippy, `cargo jackioh gate` and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass.

## Size and risks
Medium to large, hard (the AI): about 150 lines and tests, the size of #2564. Risk: probe cost per decision; capping the probes by a node budget, as Death's are, keeps the search's budget whole. A hook that only pays on a kill (Prem Panther) prices near zero against the hero, which is acceptable for a first version.

---

## Plan

_Written by `claude-6` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41324819566)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

At each decision's root, the AI prices every visible Unit on either field that has a `when_attacks` or `after_attack` hook by what its next attack would give. At the start of its controller's next turn, it plays that attack (on the enemy hero if `legal_actions` lists it, otherwise the first target listed) and subtracts the same attack made by a hookless twin. `unit_worth` adds `AI_EVAL.attack_hook` (0.5, and 0 in `GREEDY_EVAL`) times that price, inside the Brittle share. `kill_worth`, the reply's trader and `even_trade` all read `unit_worth`, so they pick the change up with no edits of their own. The result: the AI removes an enemy Wasp before a vanilla of the same stats, and it values its own Badger above a plain 2/3.

With a zero weight the evaluation stays exactly as it is today. The probes stay deterministic, never read hidden cards (R185) and are capped by `AI_ATTACK_HOOK_PROBE_NODES`. All of this is ruling R2688000.

   if swings {

4. **`evaluate.rs`, probes.** Add these after `activation_prices`:
   ```rust
   fn hookless_twin(turn: &GameState, unit: &CardInstance) -> (GameState, Vec<Keyword>) {
       let printed = face_of(turn, unit).keywords;
       let mut twin = turn.clone();
       if let Some(card) = find_instance_mut(&mut twin, &unit.id) {
           card.granted_keywords.extend(printed.iter().cloned());
           card.vanilla = true;
       }
       (twin, printed)
   }

   fn with_text_back(mut after: GameState, unit_id: &str, printed: &[Keyword]) -> GameState {
       if let Some(card) = find_instance_mut(&mut after, unit_id) {
           card.vanilla = false;
           for keyword in printed {
               if let Some(at) = card.granted_keywords.iter().position(|granted| granted == keyword) {
                   card.granted_keywords.remove(at);
               }
           }
       }
       after
   }

   fn probe_attack(legal: &[ActionBody], unit: &CardInstance) -> Option<ActionBody> {
       let hero = format!("hero-{}", unit.controller.opponent().as_str());
       let attacks: Vec<&ActionBody> = legal
           .iter()
           .filter(|action| matches!(action, ActionBody::Attack { attacker_id, .. } if *attacker_id == unit.id))
           .collect();
       let on_hero = attacks
           .iter()
           .copied()
           .find(|action| matches!(action, ActionBody::Attack { target_id, .. } if *target_id == hero));
       on_hero.or(attacks.first().copied()).cloned()
   }

   fn attack_hook_probe(
       turn: &GameState,
       unit: &CardInstance,
       attack: &ActionBody,
       counter: &dyn NodeCounter,
   ) -> Option<Option<f64>> {
       let owner = unit.controller;
       let settled = |after: &GameState| after.pending.is_none() && after.result.is_none();
       let Ok(hooked) = simulate(turn, owner, attack, counter, Prices::NONE)? else {
           return Some(None);
       };
       if !settled(&hooked) {
           return Some(None);
       }
       let (twin, printed) = hookless_twin(turn, unit);
       let Ok(plain) = simulate(&twin, owner, attack, counter, Prices::NONE)? else {
           return Some(None);
       };
       if !settled(&plain) {
           return Some(None);
       }
       let plain = with_text_back(plain, &unit.id, &printed);
       let gained = hooked.players[owner].mana.current - plain.players[owner].mana.current;
       Some(Some(
           evaluate(&hooked, owner, NextSwing::Enemy, &AI_EVAL) - evaluate(&plain, owner, NextSwing::Enemy, &AI_EVAL)
               + AI_EVAL.next_turn_mana * f64::from(gained),
       ))
   }
   ```

Copy `activation_prices`' body, with `AI_EVAL.attack_hook`, `has_attack_hook_unit`, `AI_ATTACK_HOOK_PROBE_NODES` and `attack_turns` in place of their activation counterparts.

   - Its printed keywords, as tuning leaves them, are granted so it fights as itself.

   Also add a #2688 sentence to the module doc (lines 19–29), and add R2688000 to `evaluate_priced`'s doc comment.

8. **Ruling.** Create `spec/rulings/R2688000.md` with this front matter:

   cards: "§6.2, §9.9, R185, R186, R345, R1849001, R2285000, R2285001, R2396000, R2424000, R2477000, R2564000, R2565000; Stinkyscape #75, #91, #94"

   Write the body in the shape of `R2564000.md`, with these parts:
   - **The problem:** the AI valued these Units as bodies only. No Hearthstone rule is involved, and no game plays differently.
   - **What it counts.** The two-turn walk from step 4; the target rule (hero, else first listed); the twin and its restore before scoring; the signed price; the `can_swing` gate; the Brittle share; the key by definition, face and controller; the node cap; `Prices::NONE` inside the probe; the gate numbers from step 9.
   - **What is not priced.**
     - Hand, Dormant and face-down cards.
     - Units with no legal attack.
     - An attack pair where either attack is refused, or leaves a prompt open or the game over.
     - Turns the probe does not reach, and units past the node cap.
     - A root outside the main phase or outside the seat's own turn.
   - **Approximation.**
     - The twin switches off all of the unit's text for that combat, so any other text of the unit acting in the same combat (a Death if it falls) is counted too. No shipped Unit with an attack hook has such text.
     - A hook that pays only on a kill (Prem Panther, Tmack Trav) prices about 0 against the hero.
   - **Rejected.**
     - A flat premium per hook.
     - Firing the hook alone without combat: Tmack's and the Golem's hooks read the combat's facts.
     - Probing the current turn.
     - Spawning and probing hand Units, as R2424000 does.
     - Sharing another probe's node cap.
     - Changing the engine or card scripts.

It starts `**[[R2688000]] has the AI price a unit's "when this attacks" and "after this attacks" text by its next attack, its own units' and the enemy's (issue #2688, <build date UTC>)**: …` and ends "It takes R2688000, the first number of issue #2688's block, and edits [[§9.9]]."
